answer: Clones stay expensive because every new agent must lock 340 spendable POA for 24 hours in a named ember vault shared with a randomly assigned established co-signer. At lock, a commit-reveal quartz nonce schedules twelve windows; in each, both parties jointly publish a pulse that carries a VDF output and a one-time HKDF signature bound to that nonce. A late window, a reused key, or two outputs with the same clock fingerprint slashes the vault and bars the cluster — and a colluding co-signer — from the next five epochs.
